correctness.rationale: For positive iid increments, P(S_h≤m)≤e^{am}(E e^{-aψ})^h, with E e^{-aψ}<1. This gives absolute variance summability, an integrable covariance-tail envelope, and almost surely a conditional index dependence range O(log n) by a union bound and Borel–Cantelli. At each frequency in the countably many trigonometric approximations needed, the bounded character martingale differences give the pathwise Bohr mean. For fixed h, splitting the h-step covariance innovations into residue classes modulo h+1 gives the martingale strong law for the difference from the conditional mean g_h(Y_k). Lag-continuity ensures g_h is Bohr almost periodic and the norm-continuous integral commutes with its mean. Truncating lags, prefix Cesàro convergence is uniform after division by n; omitting the last h terms of each prefix is O(H²/n) for a fixed truncation H. The ergodic collision envelope controls all longer lags simultaneously for the prefixes. Consequently conditional variances converge uniformly on the Brownian time scale to tσ², including σ²=0. Blocks of size floor(n^(1/3)) separated by O(log n) gaps are jointly independent by the setwise m-dependence assumption. Residue-class maximal inequalities make the deleted prefix sums negligible in L² after normalization. The fourth moment bound summed over normalized full blocks is O(n^(-2/3) log² n). Assign block sums to completion times: the maximal discrepancy within a block is deterministically bounded by 2K floor(n^(1/3))/sqrt(n), so the full-block conditional variance profile follows uniformly by the L² triangle inequality. The independent-array functional CLT therefore applies in J1 and uniform-probability approximation restores the original process. The separate Brownian-sign example has σ²=3−4/π at ε=0 and independent integration gives σ²≈1.8569314 at ε=1/2; these are checks of the variance formula, not the limit. Their stationary-limit covariance is the renewal-lag expectation of the Bohr mean; summing it gives the same variance on the overlap.
Whole-schedule conditional convergence here applies to almost every fixed schedule and is not another formulation of convergence under the joint law.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A joint-law scalar limit or stable convergence is weaker than almost-sure convergence of the conditional path laws. Boundedness gives L² uniform integrability but covariance almost periodicity does not give almost periodicity in distribution; conversely this record adds uniform lag-continuity. The two theorems are not restatements.

value.rationale: Inference or pathwise limit analysis with one realized observation schedule needs a conditional path law, not averaging over new schedules. The result handles arbitrarily close clusters without a minimum gap or a renewal moment and requires regularity only of lag covariances, not all marginal laws. The pathwise variance and clustering arguments together close a meaningful gap between the known annealed scalar result and such usage.
